title: 「まぁ、そういうわけで。俺とエリカ・ソルンツァリは駆け落ち。光の巫女様は夏休み明けにこう言われるのさ」
content: "Well, that's how it is. Erika Solnzali and I are eloping. Lady Light Priestess will say this after the summer vacation."
As I built up the suspense, Merseja, perhaps used to it, urged me on with a look that seemed to say, "Go ahead."
"My best friend fell in love across class lines, married her partner without permission, and eloped. So, please, Lady Priestess, pray for her future and happiness," I said.
Isn't it funny? Come on, laugh!
With just a look, I prompted Merseja, who let out a deep sigh and muttered.
"How can I laugh when you say it with that face?"
My bad.
"To use one's weakness as an excuse for one's own foolishness, and to demand concessions from the strong while hiding behind the guise of being weak, is quite a comical pride, isn't it?"
Erika Solnzali said this when she had incapacitated the eldest son of some baron who had tried to drag the Light Priestess into a night banquet hosted by his family with a string of ridiculous lies.

I returned to the guest room, giving her water as she continued to spit curses, and I recalled the eldest son of that baron, who had been thoroughly beaten to the point of needing to take a break from the academy.
Though her lips had once spat harsh words, now they only spewed curses. But as expected of Erika Solnzali, not a single drop of water spilled from her mouth.
Moreover, those lips had not only uttered harsh words.

"The reason can be anything extreme. If there is a will, it is precisely because there is a will that one can take the first step. This is the path you chose, isn't it? Therefore, only you can take that first step."
Now, go on. Do you remember when I pushed you forward like that? Well, you probably don’t. Even for the person involved, it was already a distant memory.
"So? Why is it again that you're my husband?"
As I was lost in memories of the past, feeling a bit dreamy, Merseja opened a small window and asked that. Hadn't he just said he was full of ridiculous stories?
I closed the flask and replied to Merseja.
"My father and the Prime Minister were surprisingly best friends."
From beyond the window, I heard Merseja's response, a half-hearted "Oh, really?" that suggested he didn't quite understand.
"Even among nobles, it's rare for a high marquis and a poor viscount to be friends."
"Is that so?"

Commoners probably wouldn't understand, but even among nobles, two ranks apart means they are fundamentally different. At least for me, the second son of a poor viscount family, my feelings for Erika Solnzali, the daughter of a high noble, were something I had long since given up on.
That's why the setup of a love across class lines fit the elopement perfectly, but it also meant that my Longdagger family had drawn the short straw "in bulk."
My life as a noble was essentially over, and my family would be seen as having sided with the Prime Minister, who had a fierce grudge against the royal family. It was going to be quite a challenge.
My father must have taken that into account when he disowned me, but it probably didn’t mean much.
I looked at Erika Solnzali, who was still blankly spitting curses.
Now, names of other high nobles who had likely been involved alongside the prince had been added to her list.
As expected of a talented woman. Even after being told of her exile and immediately being exiled, she accurately cursed the right targets after just one explanation.

Truly, our talents are different. I trembled at the fortune of being able to be by the side of a woman I had considered unattainable, even if only in name as her husband. Just that was enough for me to throw my life away.
For a moment, I thought about what I would do if she remained like this for the rest of her life.
But when I imagined it, it surprisingly seemed easy. No matter the state, Erika Solnzali was beautiful.
I could spend my life taking care of her while she smiled.
Traveling the world with Erika, who continued to curse, might not be so bad after all.
No... this might actually be fun?
As I imagined traveling the world with Erika, Merseja called out to me.
We were wandering through a vast forest in a country far south of Faltarl, and I felt a bit irritated.
"Ah, husband, I have something to discuss."
Saying that, Merseja slowed the carriage down.
What is it? I thought as I leaned closer to the small window to talk to the coachman.
"There's a chance there might be bandits ahead, though it's still a ways off."
"Huh? Bandits this close to the royal capital?"

I was surprised; we had left the royal capital eight hours ago in the early morning. We were using the main road, and since we had very few belongings for a noble's travel, the carriage was moving at a decent speed. It was practically right under the nose of the royal capital.
Although I was currently exiled, was the security of our country really that bad?
"No, it's probably because we're close."
Merseja said, looking at a small forest along the still distant road.

According to Merseja, the road extending west from the royal capital was often used by merchant carriages carrying trade goods, and it was the furthest point one would have to pass when leaving the royal capital.
The knight order of the royal capital was well aware of this area and patrolled it thoroughly. However, that also meant that if the timing was right, it was an excellent spot for banditry.
"Right now, no other carriages are passing, so if there are really bandits, they might target us."
"I see."
I took in Merseja's implication that this was a carriage that looked like it belonged to a wealthy person.

Since my home was in the royal capital, I had little experience being outside of it, so I had no reason to doubt the words of an experienced adventurer. Well, the truth was that my family was too poor to have ever traveled. I pulled the sword I had leaned against and spoke to Merseja.
"By the way, what's your adventurer rank?"
"Rank 6."

I see, as expected of the Prime Minister. He must not have spared any expense for his daughter. He had hired the highest rank he could afford for continuous employment. If someone could operate as a rank 6 adventurer in Faltarl, they were at least half a monster themselves.

While the occurrence of monsters in Faltarl Kingdom is lower than in other countries, the monsters that do appear tend to be exceptionally strong, making it difficult to continuously hire adventurers.
It's often more profitable to hunt monsters than to take on quests.
Rank 6 is the best rank you can hope for in terms of finances, as well as the likelihood that the person is available.
By the way, in my Longdagger family, even hiring a rank 6 adventurer continuously would be impossible, financially speaking.
"Do you know how many there are?"
"There are six in the forest to the right of the road."
Even from quite a distance, Merseja confidently stated. I see, being rank 6 is no joke.
"Well, they should be weak."
Merseja muttered, looking distant, as if they wouldn't even be able to break through the carriage's barrier.
I hung the sword I had pulled to my waist and climbed onto the driver's seat.
"Why are you getting out?"
Merseja seemed to be saying, "You're the target of protection."
Ignoring that, I asked, "Should we cut through?"
I suggested, recalling the few "quests" I had taken. Bandits are usually desperate people on the brink of starvation.
It's not uncommon to find emaciated bandits who can't even catch up to a loaded carriage.
If they come after us, we can just scare them off a bit. If they are monsters, we need to wipe them out, but against humans, intimidation is usually enough.
"Well, let's do that."
Merseja looked at me as if he wanted to say something, then increased the speed of the carriage.
Due to our poverty, I had only ever ridden in a carriage for "quests," but I could tell that the carriage prepared by the Prime Minister for his daughter was a good one.
Despite being a single-horse carriage, it was moving at quite a speed. Even though it was on a well-maintained road, the lack of jolting was astonishing.
The speed of the carriage seemed unexpected for the hidden bandits, as they rushed out from the forest to block the road.
There were six of them, all men. Even from a distance, their shabby clothing and thin bodies were apparent, and they held swords that looked rusty and unkempt, likely picked up or stolen.
I could acknowledge their courage in stepping in front of a speeding carriage, but if this continued, they would end up seriously injured or dead.
As we got within about fifty feet, the men's faces told me they weren't going to run away.
Are they really that stupid? Just as I thought that, it happened.
"Merseja! Stop!"
"Stopping!"
Merseja seemed to have realized it almost simultaneously and shouted as he slowed the horses. A carriage cannot stop suddenly. It will inevitably continue moving due to inertia.

If we try to stop too abruptly, the horses could get injured. Injuries can be healed with healing magic, but if they die, there's nothing we can do. We were moving at quite a speed, so the chances of that happening were high.
Merseja clicked his tongue as he handled the reins. In other words, it was too late.
I took a deep breath, confirming the flow of magic power throughout my body.
"I'll go!"
"What did you say!?"

Ignoring Merseja's voice that sounded like he was saying, "No way," I kicked off the driver's seat and leaped over the horses, moving forward. As my toes touched the ground, I unleashed body enhancement magic.
One of the men blocking the road shouted in panic.
"Stop!"
The man who shouted looked at my face, bewildered, wondering why I was so close.

I hesitated for a moment when I saw the "collars" around the men's necks. This was why Merseja chose to stop the carriage, and why I had jumped out. The possibility that they were just good farmers being forced to do this under duress crossed my mind.
However, I felt relieved that there was likely no cause for concern.

The men's clothes had stains that looked like blood. Such stains could easily be cleaned with purification magic, even by a child. The fact that they were deliberately left there meant they were using it to intimidate.
Nine times out of ten, they were not decent people.
Well, the carriage was now only about ten feet away. Regardless of who these guys were, I had no other choice. Erika was in the carriage.
In other words, I just wanted an excuse for my first kill.
The man reflexively swung his sword down at me.
He had no proper sword training, and there was no distance to speak of. I grabbed the man's wrist and threw him toward the forest.
The man soared over the trees and fell into the woods, leaving the other five dumbfounded.
If they had put up some sort of decent counterattack, I might have felt a bit better about it.
No, it probably wouldn't have changed anything.
I would have likely done the same regardless of who they were, even if they were unarmed women and children. The magic power leaking from the collars told me they were already activated.
I tossed the men into the forest without allowing them any resistance.
By the time I threw the last man, the carriage was only about five feet away.
Before the man could clear the trees, I hurriedly hid behind the carriage.
"Husband! Get down!"
I'm already down! I shouted back in my mind to Merseja.
The carriage's barrier had already been manually raised to maximum strength, and unless we were extremely close, the passenger carriage wouldn't budge.
Oh, the horses.

Just as I remembered the horses, the last man I threw exploded in mid-air. Almost simultaneously, an explosion erupted from the forest. Debris and small stones pelted against the carriage's barrier, and the horses looked at it with expressions that seemed to say, "What is this?"
As expected of the Prime Minister. He had ensured the horses were protected, and they were well-trained.
"Husband!"
At Merseja's voice, I clung to the carriage. Instead of going to the driver's seat, I climbed onto the roof to secure a better view.
"What kind of bandits are these!"
I couldn't help but complain as Merseja drove the carriage at full speed.
"Isn't it more likely that they are not just failed assassins, but rather traitors to the state!? Using magical tools for preventing the escape of criminals, human bombs—these guys are not sane!"
Certainly, Erika's beauty could topple a nation.
"If Erika Solnzali wanted to overthrow the state, I'd be fighting on the front lines by now!"
"Are you an idiot!? You were already an idiot for throwing a human bomb without hesitation!"
Merseja freely called me an idiot. I admit I was foolish, but I thought it was only natural to fight for Erika.
"By the way, what's your rank, husband!?"
Merseja shouted over the noise of the carriage.
"I'm rank 4! It's busy attending the academy!"
After blurting that out, I thought, oh no.
Adventurers are essentially armed commoners.
Thus, unlike the church, which has no interest in secular power, the relationship between adventurers and nobles is often tense.
The academy in the royal capital itself started from a somewhat arrogant idea that if commoners can wield weapons, nobles should become even stronger.
So, being a noble who is also an adventurer, like me, is something that requires caution. If I casually say I'm a noble adventurer, it could attract unnecessary resentment.
As I thought I had messed up, Merseja spoke up.
"Don't worry! I don't have any issues with nobles being adventurers!"
His voice was unexpectedly considerate.
"More like, it feels like 'of course!'"

What does "of course" mean? From the perspective of Merseja, a rank 6 adventurer, my movements must seem ordinary. Well, it's true that unfortunately, I am not a person overflowing with talent, and rank 4 is just that kind of rank. While I was thinking that, the carriage emerged from the forest.
As soon as my view opened up, I saw it.
"To the right front!"
Merseja shouted, likely indicating a reaction he picked up with some detection skill.
A line of magic power clearly targeted the carriage. It was a distinct magic filled with hostility and intent to kill.
"A spell is coming!"
"What!?"
Merseja, who probably couldn't see the line of magic targeting the carriage, raised a confused voice. Along with Merseja's voice, I heard the sound of air being sliced.
"Flame Spear! One!"
I only stated the type of incoming magic and looked down.
No way! Merseja shouted and turned his face away from the barrier. The flame spear hit the barrier and exploded. I witnessed the Prime Minister's seriousness as the barrier remained unyielding.
Raising my face, which had been lowered to avoid the light of the explosion, I checked my surroundings.
"Merseja! How many enemies are there!?"
"Four! One of them is dangerous!"
A dangerous opponent, as described by a rank 6 adventurer. What a lavish bandit.
Here I am, the second son of a poor viscount family, and a noble lady who is about to be exiled! If they want money, they should be attacking merchant carriages.
Or perhaps──.

Three men jumped out from the side of the carriage, clearly using body enhancement. A barrier device that could be mounted on a carriage cannot be set to allow only specific individuals inside. If this continued, they would board the carriage.
"If you can use that much, then work seriously! You idiots!"
I shouted angrily while unleashing body enhancement magic to deal with the three men.
"Are you okay? Senior?"
As I corrected the unique sensation of my thoughts and movements being misaligned while using high-intensity body enhancement, I peeked out from the roof to check on Merseja's safety.
"I thought the head of the bandits would be crushed by a thrown dagger, and then suddenly, humans came flying in a group of three. What on earth did you do?"

I had thrown a dagger at the bandit leader, who was aiming for Merseja, and noticed that the leader was wearing the same collar as before, so I threw the other two at him to distance them from the carriage.
"No, it's fine. No need to explain."
I was about to explain when Merseja cut me off.
"Even if you were rank cheating, that's just terrible──"
Just as Merseja muttered in disbelief, an explosion occurred behind the carriage.
It must have been the previous bandits. Merseja made a strange face.
"Things are a mess over there too."
Indeed. I deeply agreed with Merseja's words. In just one day since leaving the royal capital, I had thrown several people and every one of them exploded.
For some reason, the value of human life around me was plummeting.
Is life truly something that exceeds imagination? Well, even if it's a farce, I am to become the husband of Erika Solnzali. In that case, anything goes.
"I think your movements are the most chaotic, husband."
For some reason, Merseja looked exasperated.
"I can't use magic properly, but I have a bit of confidence in body enhancement and healing magic."
"Don't say something chaotic with a serious face, please."
I answered seriously, only to be further exasperated.
Well, whatever. The enemies are still remaining.
"More importantly, can we escape?"
At my question, Merseja put away his exasperation and gave me a sarcastic look.
"If they can't catch up to a big box carriage, then we should be fine."
I see, that was a foolish question.
I locked onto the carriage directly, reflecting on the murderous intent radiating from the magic power.
I am not good at fighting humans, or rather, I have little experience. I find it more suited to deal with monsters.
"It would be easier to punch an ogre barehanded."
"Please use tools if you're human."
Indeed, I could see the last remaining figure, who was not hiding at all. Ignoring Merseja's sarcastic remark, I said, "Well then, I'm going."
I declared that I had no intention of letting them escape as I looked at the attacker standing confidently in the middle of the road.
"He's an enemy of the woman I love, you know?"
Just thinking that made me feel like I could do anything.
I drew my sword from its sheath and increased the intensity of my body enhancement.
"If there is a next life, I’ll teach you to choose your job better."
I charged toward the attacker.
Behind me, I heard Merseja mutter, "Is this what it means to be 'Longdagger, unworthy of his status?'"
When a skilled adventurer uses body enhancement for high-speed movement, their footsteps are said to leave no trace. That is a well-known story.
Unfortunately, as an inexperienced person, I kicked up a storm of dirt as I ran.
For the attacker, it must have been unexpected that I was coming out from the carriage's barrier, as I noticed the line of magic aimed at the carriage waver for a moment.
To hesitate means to be overly complacent, doesn’t it?

I increased my speed and closed the distance to the attacker. My enhanced eyes caught the attacker's face. Clad in a robe covering their entire body, with a hood and a mask obscuring their face, they looked suspicious enough that I might have attacked even if they approached me in a non-threatening manner.

As I drew closer, the attacker seemed to have made up their mind, focusing their intent on the carriage. The line of magic surged with hostility and determination. This was not the magic meant to assist in boarding the carriage.
A serious spell was coming.
I could see the attacker move about a hundred feet away. I wanted to get closer before they could cast.
I wished I could cast some sort of magic myself. Unfortunately, I could only manage basic life magic, which is said to be something even children can do if taught.
The quality of the magic line changed.
The thoughts of "it's coming" and "it's here" surged simultaneously.
I could have trusted the performance of the carriage prepared by the Prime Minister, but today I had relied too much on my father-in-law.
The setup for our elopement was made to ensure the Light Priestess's heart wouldn't cloud, but even as the husband in this farce, I had my pride.
Suddenly, words I wanted to say came out of my mouth for no reason.
"Father-in-law! Please give me your daughter!"
I couldn't believe those words came out of my mouth.
As I doubted my sanity, I realized my actions were becoming increasingly erratic.
I scooped up the cobblestones of the road with my sword and threw them into the path of the approaching flame spear.

The flame spear made contact with the cobblestones. An explosion occurred right in front of me. I crouched as low as I could, but my eardrums burst in an instant, my brain shook violently, and I realized I had gone blind.
